Byomkesh.description: The protagonist and sharp-eyed truth-seeker who investigates the murder at Karalibabu's house.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates the events and assists in the investigation.

Bidhubabu.description: The Deputy Commissioner of Police known for his pompous and ostentatious manner.

Karalibabu.description: A wealthy, irascible, and childless widower who frequently changed his will and was eventually murdered.

Motilal.description: One of Karalibabu's nephews, initially suspected of the murder due to his quarrelsome nature.

Makhanlal.description: Another nephew of Karalibabu, known for his indulgence in drugs but not considered as degenerate as Motilal.

Phonibhushan.description: Karalibabu's lame nephew, ultimately revealed as the murderer; well-read but embittered by his disability.

Satyaboti.description: A strong-willed and intelligent young woman devoted to her brother Sukumar and related to Karalibabu's wife.

Sukumar.description: Satyaboti's brother and a medical student who was the initial beneficiary of Karalibabu's last will.

Putiram.description: Byomkesh and Ajit's servant, who prepares tea for them.

Dalim.description: A woman from the red-light area, with whom Motilal claims to have spent the night.

Calcutta.description: The city (now Kolkata) where the story is set, reflecting the urban Bengali milieu.

Chitra.description: A cinema hall in Calcutta where Sukumar claims to have watched a film the night of the murder.

Mirzapuri.description: Refers to Mirzapur, a region known for its carpets; a Mirzapuri carpet is mentioned in Karalibabu's room.

Gray’s Anatomy.description: A famous medical textbook, found in Sukumar's room and relevant to the murder method.

Cornwallis Street.description: A street in Calcutta, used as a landmark in the narrative.

CID.description: Criminal Investigation Department, a specialized branch of the police in India.

Christian calendar.description: Refers to the Gregorian calendar, used to date the will in the story.

kurta.description: A traditional Indian long shirt worn by men.

chawl.description: A type of low-cost, communal housing found in Indian cities, typically consisting of small rooms along a corridor.

lakhs.description: An Indian unit equal to one hundred thousand (100,000), often used to denote sums of money.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

teapoy.description: A small table, often used to serve tea.

sari.description: A traditional Indian garment worn by women, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

probate.description: The legal process of validating a will and administering the estate of the deceased.
